newsitem.title: USA: Old America to post charges in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Old America to post charges in Q4.

text.p: Old America Stores Inc said Friday that it will incur pretax charges for the fourth fiscal quarter ending Jan. 31, 1997, totaling about $7.8 million before taxes.

The charges result from (1) markdowns related to merchandise that will not be carried in the future; (2) costs associated with the relocation and/or closing of up to 16 stores that do not meet the company's site size and/or location criteria; (3) the write-down of the net book value of certain store equipment replaced during the recent installation of the company's point-of-sale system; and (4) severance costs related to certain management changes.

Richard Tredinnick, president and chief executive officer, said, "With the SKU-level information we are now obtaining from Old America's new point-of-sale and inventory systems, we can better identify our best-selling merchandise and estimate rates-of-sale. This has helped us to improve in-stock positions for these items and optimize our merchandise mix.

"We've also identified certain merchandise that will not be replenished in the future. We've decided to liquidate this merchandise as quickly as possible to enhance our ability to properly configure our stores for higher traffic and better customer service."

Tredinnick said that all nine of the new Old America stores opened in the second half of 1996 feature the company's new product assortment and softer, more customer-friendly look and feel. "These stores were opened in better, higher-traffic locations than were selected in the past, and the results thus far have been very encouraging," he said.

"We've also addressed certain stores whose present locations have limited revenue growth potential and do not meet our requirements for size and/or site quality. We are evaluating a number of stores for relocation or closure as leases expire in 1997," Tredinnick said.
